newsitem.title: MEXICO: Guatemala ups dumping tariff of Mexico cement firm.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala ups dumping tariff of Mexico cement firm.

text.p: Guatemala said Wednesday it would more than double to 89.54 percent the tariff charged on cement imports from the privately held Mexican firm Cruz Azul, claiming it continues to dump cement on the Guatemalan market.
In August, Guatemala imposed a 38.72 percent tariff on Cruz Azul cement.

"We concluded that there has been unfair trade practices according to norms established by the World Trade Organization," Economy Minister Juan Mauricio Wurmser told a news conference. Wurmser said an investigation showed Cruz Azul cement was sold in Guatemala at wholesale prices lower than in Mexico and imports of low-priced Cruz Azul cement harmed Guatemala's only cement producer, Cementos Progreso.
Cruz Azul is overshadowed in the Mexican market by the huge Mexican companies Cemex and Apasco.
Wurmser said Cruz Azul's share of the Guatemalan market soared to 30 percent from one percent in 1995 and that 90 percent of the cement imported to Guatemala comes from Cruz Azul.
